free_tier.stated: HKT.NAT.500M.VPS: 1 vCPU, 0.25 GB RAM, 8 GB NVMe, shared 500 Mbps, 300 GB traffic, 1 shared HKT IPv4, 1 HKT IPv6 SLAAC, 5 custom NAT ports, Debian 12 only. [translated]

chaining: WG over the IPv6 SLAAC address would avoid the NAT port allocation entirely, if a user's network has IPv6.
binding_note: 300 GB is about 0.27 TiB, so the byte allowance fails first, at roughly a quarter of the test.

identity_cost.detail: Not described in the post; NAT VPS signups of this class typically take an email plus a panel account.

reliability_note: Debian 12 only; a 0.25 GB RAM box is tight for a WG plus anything else.
confidence_note: A marketplace post quoting the plan; the vendor page was not read. Vendor confirmation would raise the rung.

evidence.proved: 300 GB traffic, 5 custom NAT ports, 500 Mbps shared, free machine

notes: Explicit custom NAT ports plus IPv6 SLAAC is the shape that lets WG work without a public IPv4. The 300 GB cap is the blocker. The post is a resale of a free machine, which is itself evidence that these free NAT boxes get traded.

extras.wg_detail: Root on a NAT VPS with 5 custom NAT ports and a routed IPv6; WG can bind a port from the allocated set, or ride IPv6 directly.
extras.transit_note: Hong Kong host carries the traffic.
